newsitem.title: UK: Top UK pension fund managers post poor Q2 returns.
newsitem.headline: Top UK pension fund managers post poor Q2 returns.

text.p: Several heavyweight UK pension fund managers sharply underperformed the industry in the second quarter and over the past year, a survey released on Wednesday showed.

The survey which measures the performance of UK pooled pension funds, showed Mercury Asset Management, PDFM, Prudential and Gartmore all lagging the average industry return in the second quarter, as well as over six and twelve months in the mixed funds including property.
It was conducted by Combined Actuarial Performance Services (CAPS).
Schroders, which managed to come in at the industry median of 5.8 percent in the second quarter, was also below average over six and 12 months.

And the poor recent performances have started to seep into the more important long term performance figures, with traditional top-ten performers Mercury and Schroders falling to 20th and 14th place respectively in five year rolling returns.

The survey showed Mercury's 4.2 billion sterling Managed Fund Service returned 3.9 percent in the second quarter, ranking it at 62 out of 70 funds measured, while it came in at 68th out of 70 over six and 12 months.

PDFM, with assets of 1.1 billion sterling in the sector, was 65th in the second quarter, 67th over six months and 55th over a year. Prudential, with 1.84 billion sterling, was 55th over six months and 42d over 12.

CAPS said Fuji, J Rothschild and Bank of Ireland mixed-with-property funds had all moved into the top 10 of five-year rolling returns after markedly overweighing North American and European equities in the last year.
Top performing mixed-with-property funds in the quarter were Royal and Sun Alliance, Edinburgh Fund Managers and Baillie Gifford with eight percent each.
Among the worst second quarter performers were Swiss Life, Ivory & Sime and Glasgow Investment Managers.
But Glasgow Investment Managers was the top performer over five years, with Brittania and Morgan Grenfell the only funds with over one billion sterling to register in the top 10.
